# mbmm

**mbmm** implements the **Mechanistic Bayes Mixture Model (MBMM)**
framework described by Do, McCarthy, and Rogers (2026) in *Mechanistic
Bayes Mixture Models*.

MBMM estimates how a covariate changes the probability of a latent
biological state expressed through a longitudinal mechanistic
trajectory. Examples include productive infection versus
non-establishment, or a positive durable antibody gain versus no durable
gain.

Rather than reducing a trajectory to a thresholded label, MBMM evaluates
each participant against populations of mechanistic trajectories. A
covariate-dependent logistic gate supplies the prior state probability,
and the trajectory evidence and gate combine into a posterior
responsibility. Participants whose trajectories do not settle the state
contribute according to that uncertainty instead of being forced into a
class.

The package is model-agnostic. Users may supply any positive trajectory
function with arguments **time** and **theta**, including a custom ODE
solved with **deSolve**. Built-in eclipse-phase viral and prime-boost
antibody models are included for the manuscript examples.

The current package provides:

- censoring-aware participant-by-trajectory likelihoods;
- integration over latent timing offsets and other nuisance coordinates;
- entropy-penalised kinetic-population estimation;
- independent-donor and exact leave-one-out bank construction;
- Route I state-specific reference banks;
- Route II restriction to a prespecified parameter-space region;
- logistic gate fitting, including optional Firth penalisation;
- likelihood-ratio or penalised-objective statistics with permutation
  tests;
- diagnostic plots for banks, responsibilities, and fitted gates; and
- fully synthetic examples with known truth and executable recovery
  checks.

## Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("linhdo154/MBMM")
```

Then load the package:

``` r

library(mbmm)
```

## Getting started

The package has four linked vignettes:

- [Should I use
  MBMM?](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/articles/mbmm.html) explains
  suitable scientific questions, required assumptions, core functions,
  diagnostics, and reporting conditions.
- [Bring your own
  ODE](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/articles/custom-ode.html)
  reconstructs the built-in models from scratch, shows both familiar
  parameter boxes and identifiable bank designs, and fits a custom
  constant-beta HIV model.
- [Route I](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/articles/pipeline.html)
  uses an independent pure reference bank in a productive-infection
  simulation and checks recovery against known truth.
- [Route II](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/articles/sdy2354.html)
  defines a durable-gain state as a prespecified parameter region, uses
  exact leave-one-out banks, and checks recovery against known truth.

The complete package website is available at:

<https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/>

## Minimal workflow

``` r

# Score each participant against each candidate trajectory
LL <- trajectory_loglik(
  obs, candidates, trajectory = my_model, sigma = 0.3
)

# Estimate a kinetic population from an appropriate donor likelihood matrix
bank <- fit_bank(LL_donors, lambda = 1)

# Form the two class likelihoods
l1 <- class_loglik(LL, bank$weights)
l0 <- background_loglik(obs, sigma = 0.3)

# Fit and test the covariate gate
fit <- fit_gate(l1, l0, X)
test <- gate_test(l1, l0, X, B = 999)
```

The bank used to score a participant must not have been fitted or
screened using that participant’s measurements. Use a separate donor
sample or exact cross-fitting with **bank_loo()**.

## Data and reproduction

No participant-level or packaged SDY2354 dataset is distributed with
mbmm. To reproduce the manuscript’s SDY2354 analysis, obtain SDY2354
directly from ImmPort under its user agreement and provide the prepared
table to **inst/reproduce/sdy2354_table3.R**.

**simulate_mbmm()** supplies a fully synthetic Route I cohort with known
latent states.

## Citation

To obtain the recommended package citation in R:

``` r

citation("mbmm")
```

The methodological framework is described in:

> Do, L., McCarthy, J., and Rogers, B. (2026).  
> *Mechanistic Bayes Mixture Models.*

# Package index

## Likelihood

Turning measurements into evidence for a state

- [`obs_loglik()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/obs_loglik.md)
  : Log-likelihood of one measurement under a trajectory
- [`trajectory_loglik()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/trajectory_loglik.md)
  : Participant-by-candidate log-likelihood matrix
- [`background_loglik()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/background_loglik.md)
  : Background (class-0) log-likelihood at a fraction of the assay limit
- [`class_loglik()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/class_loglik.md)
  : Class likelihood from a bank

## Building the likelihood over shared points

Integrating out what the question is not about

- [`pool_marginal()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/pool_marginal.md)
  : Integrate a nuisance pool out of a candidate likelihood
- [`jitter_marginal()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/jitter_marginal.md)
  : Integrate a calibration offset along a grid coordinate

## The kinetic population

Estimating the bank, and keeping it honest

- [`fit_bank()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/fit_bank.md)
  : Estimate bank weights by entropy-penalised maximum likelihood
- [`bank_loo()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/bank_loo.md)
  : Leave-one-out banks
- [`screen_candidates()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/screen_candidates.md)
  : Screen candidates to the ones participants actually support
- [`screen_positive()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/screen_positive.md)
  : Reject candidates whose trajectory is not positive
- [`profile_sigma()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/profile_sigma.md)
  : Profile the residual scale
- [`restrict_bank()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/restrict_bank.md)
  : Restrict a bank to a region of parameter space (Route II)

## The gate

Covariate association with the latent state

- [`fit_gate()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/fit_gate.md)
  : Fit the covariate gate by EM
- [`gate_test()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/gate_test.md)
  : Test a covariate effect in the gate

## Mechanistic models

- [`eclipse_trajectory()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/eclipse_trajectory.md)
  : Eclipse-phase target-cell-limited viral kinetics
- [`eclipse_design()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/eclipse_design.md)
  : Candidate design on identifiable viral coordinates
- [`andraud_trajectory()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/andraud_trajectory.md)
  : Reduced prime-boost antibody kinetics
- [`andraud_levels()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/andraud_levels.md)
  : Class coordinate for a prime-boost question
- [`amp_to_flux()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/amp_to_flux.md)
  [`flux_to_amp()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/amp_to_flux.md)
  : Convert between amplitudes and production fluxes

## Simulation

- [`simulate_mbmm()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/simulate_mbmm.md)
  : Simulate a cohort with a latent kinetic state

## Visualisation

Seeing the kinetic population and checking simulation recovery

- [`plot_bank()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/plot_bank.md)
  : Plot a weighted mechanistic trajectory bank
- [`plot_responsibility()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/plot_responsibility.md)
  : Plot posterior responsibilities against simulated truth
- [`plot_gate()`](https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/reference/plot_gate.md)
  : Plot a fitted covariate gate
